images.title: A negative exponent moves below the bar
images.purpose: Shows 2 with exponent −4 rewritten as 1 over 2⁴, which is 1/16.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. Three expressions in a row across the centre joined by equals signs, with one curved arrow showing the power moving below the bar.
images.exact_structure: Left: a large '2⁻⁴' with the 2 in teal (#0072B2) and the raised exponent in amber (#E69F00); the raised minus is a true minus sign, not a hyphen. An equals sign. Middle: a fraction with '1' above a short bar and '2⁴' below it; the 2 in teal (#0072B2), the 4 in amber (#E69F00). One curved amber (#E69F00) arrow from the exponent on the left down to the 2⁴ below the bar. An equals sign. Right: the fraction '1' over '16' inside a reddish purple (#CC79A7) rounded box. Exactly 2 fractions, 2 equals signs, 1 arrow, 1 box.

images.takeaway: A negative exponent means one over the positive power: 2 to the power −4 is 1/16.
images.description: Shows 2 with exponent −4 rewritten as 1 over 2⁴, which is 1/16.
images.context: 2 to the power −4 is 1/2⁴ = 1/16. The sign of the base stays: (−5) to the power −3 is 1/(−5)³ = −1/125.

image_decisions.why: Moving the power below the bar is the one rule this concept teaches.
